head: cd85ce80580c82df6222f2c7d7df7a5b4eea4b89
non_blocking: Raise paths only partly pinned (T02c-review2-10 R4, T02c-review2-11 R5, T02c-review2-12): deleting the up-front bar_segments call in songform._section_phrases (R4), or moving both up-front checks after the identity and duplicate refusals (R5), passes the gate. Witnesses: under R4 an all-instrumental form over an off-bar meter map assembles; under R4 or R5 an off-bar map plus a SongSpec naming another revision refuses song_melody_mismatch instead of raising. The codes are pinned (each {'invalid': ...} vector places a phrase and position() re-validates the map), but README's 'a source the time model cannot measure ... is an input error, not a refusal' is not pinned for a form with no phrase or for its precedence over earlier refusals. Add {'invalid': 'meter_change_inside_bar'} for an all-instrumental form over an off-bar map and one pairing an unmeasurable source with a SongSpec mismatch. Low risk: melody.wellformed rejects such a stored record.

Meter claim, verified in effect: a valid map can put a meter change in a phrase's trailing rest only after an earlier change inside the phrase's span (the first change after the anchor lands on a bar line of the phrase's meter, hence before its end), which already refuses meter_conflict; a phrase with one meter up to its end meets a trailing meter change only off a bar line, which raises meter_change_inside_bar. Proof plus 3,050,104 exhaustive pairs and 75 seeded pairs (T02c-review2-09); reverting only the meter range is an equivalent mutant (0 of 4031 outcomes change, T02c-review2-08). The paraphrase 'cannot occur for any map passing bar_segments' is slightly too strong (68 seeded inputs place an on-bar change in a trailing rest, always after an in-span change); the meter half of the fix is behaviour-neutral, kept for symmetry with the README.

Rounding: all 7 assembled songform end_frame values are exact, so half-up rounding is exercised only by tempo.json; no fixture.tempo vector pins tempo_segments_invalid through ticks_to_frames (only assembly's {'invalid': ...} vector does).
contracts/README.md lost its trailing newline (the head ends with '.', the base ended with a newline); the lint does not flag it.

Still open from round 1: rule tightenings also apply to 1.0.0 records (bar-line meter rule, exact inheritance of a non-null 1.0 lineage; disclosed and vacuous, 0 of 19 tempo maps at dee28e2 has more than one meter segment, T02c-review2-16); annotation-driven fields manifest; smells (rules.py:1051 re-derives the bar-line rule, test_songform.py setUp/run_cli copy test_vector_discovery.py, HYMN_* restates the world hymn - re-verified equal, T02c-review2-15 - and tuple-typed time and segments); no GLOSSARY entry for 'pickup' or 'chord symbol' (disclosed).

Pre-existing, outside the diff (follow-up): lane.record_eligible compares a transcription's eligible_lanes with its transcriber's but never its license_chain; a Basic Pitch transcription carrying pYIN's chain on both the source and its 1.1.0 assembled copy still yields 0 findings (T02c-review2-17). Lanes cannot widen.

Size: 823 added hand-written Python lines (720 non-blank: reference 268, vector data 436, generator hooks 57, tests 62) plus 212 schema, 34 manifest and 102 README lines; the fix alone is about 150 hand-written lines. Over the ~400 aim; it did not impair review.

Merge order with #128 (now 9742d88) and #130 (now 8361db1), both on dee28e2. #130 already carries #131's fields mechanism: MANIFEST_KEYS {version, scope, consumers, fields, records, pending} with fields required, version 2, scope 'vector-kinds and record fields', added_fields() with the old regex 'added in 1\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+', fields {}, and {**consumers, **fields} validated through check_tickets(known_tickets) plus check_records; #131 checks version 1 and scope 'vector-kinds and added fields'. Whichever of #130/#131 lands second: keep #130's discovery structure; one agreed scope string (e.g. 'vector-kinds, record fields and added fields') in consumers.json, discovery and both README paragraphs; adopt #131's ADDED regex 'added in 1\.[1-9][0-9]*\.[0-9]+'; fields = #131's two entries; consumers = the union (binding, songform, meter, and midi once #128 lands) with each list unchanged; records and pending as #130 (melody-spec and song-spec stay pending); keep both test files (#131's subtests match 'missing', 'orphan' and 'unknown consumer ticket slug', the last contained in #130's 'duplicate or unknown consumer ticket slug'); keep both generate_fixtures.py hooks, regenerate, and re-prove byte identity plus validate.py -v. #128's _check_order (midi.py:74-80) calls timemodel._segments, which #131 renames to the public timemodel.tempo_segments (raising TimeModelError('tempo_segments_invalid')); whichever of #128/#131 lands second must switch that call (its except ValueError still catches TimeModelError) and #128's README:163 reference, or the second branch fails with AttributeError. Keep the 'MIDI round trip (T02d)', 'SongForm assembly (T02c)' and 'Evidence-binding inputs (T02b)' README sections, merge the 'Not covered yet' line (#131 reflowed it; #128 drops 'the MIDI round trip') and add consumers['fixture.midi']. #128 already refuses an off-bar time signature (MidiRefusal meter_change_inside_bar), closing the round-1 item; #131's PR body still lists it as needed (stale line).

Evidence hygiene (implementer folder): SHA256SUMS-fixes verifies, but the round-1 SHA256SUMS no longer does because probes.py was overwritten in place at 20:45 (round-1 line 8f6039c3..., file now 93739fd3..., the SHA256SUMS-fixes hash), so the round-1 probe script is no longer on disk although its logs are; version evidence files instead of overwriting them.

Base drift: integration advanced from dee28e2 to 0e02d72 during this review (#127, S01 public-build decision and expansion trials, merged 2026-11-08T03:03Z; no file overlap with #131; tickets.json grows to 108 tickets and every slug #131 uses still exists; neither #128 nor #130 has landed), so #131 is BEHIND. A local trial merge of 0e02d72 into cd85ce8 (never pushed, noreply identity) keeps the reviewed patch-id 09e0de2b8daedab41b949dc7c1fcad06cce90cc0 and passes the full local gate and validate.py -v (T02c-review2-22, -22b). This review carries to an updated head while that patch-id is unchanged.
